posts.title: RAPID Charity Hosts Educational Seminar on CSS and PMS Competitive Exams
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: As part of RAPID Charity’s ongoing commitment to professional mentorship and youth empowerment, an introductory educational webinar was recently organized for RAPID scholarship students and alumni.
posts.body:
## Introduction & Overview

As part of RAPID Charity’s ongoing commitment to professional mentorship and youth empowerment, an introductory educational webinar was recently organized for RAPID scholarship students and alumni. Focused on navigating Pakistan's prestigious civil service examinations, the session provided students from multiple colleges with a comprehensive roadmap for pursuing careers as Grade 17 gazetted officers through the CSS (Federal) and PMS (Provincial) competitive examinations.

The session was led by esteemed RAPID alumna Farah Tariq, an Assistant Director in Punjab's Environment Protection Department, who shared firsthand guidance, strategic insights, and practical preparation advice drawn from her own successful journey. To ensure maximum accessibility and clarity for all attendees, the seminar was conducted in a bilingual (Urdu and English) format.

## CSS vs. PMS: Understanding the Key Distinctions

The webinar kicked off with a breakdown of the two major civil service pathways available to Pakistani graduates:

- **CSS (Central Superior Services):** Conducted federally by the FPSC (Federal Public Service Commission). Successful candidates are allocated to various occupational groups and can be posted anywhere across Pakistan.
- **PMS (Provincial Management Services):** Conducted by respective provincial commissions (such as PPSC in Punjab) or known as the Combined Competitive Exam (CCE) in Sindh, leading to provincial administrative roles.
- **Common Goal:** Both competitive routes lead directly to prestigious Grade 17 gazetted officer positions, such as Assistant Commissioner, Section Officer, or Assistant Director.

## Key Insights on CSS Eligibility & Structure

Farah Tariq walked students through the rigorous structure of the CSS examination, highlighting critical updates and requirements:

- **Eligibility Criteria:** Open to Pakistani citizens holding at least a Bachelor's degree (minimum second division) between the ages of 21 to 30 years (with a 2-year relaxation for existing government servants). Candidates have a maximum of 3 total attempts.
- **The MPT (Preliminary Screening Test):** An MCQ-based screening filter featuring 200 questions with a passing threshold of 66 marks. Notably, attempts at the MPT do not count against the candidate's three official CSS attempt limits.
- **Written Examination (1,200 Total Marks):** Comprises 6 compulsory subjects (English Essay, English Précis & Composition, General Science & Ability, Current Affairs, Pakistan Affairs, and Islamic Studies/Comparative Religion) and 6 optional subjects chosen across structured groups. Passing thresholds are strictly 40% for compulsory and 33% for optional papers.
- **Recent Exam Format Changes:** Highlighting a crucial recent update, each compulsory paper is now held on a separate day (a shift from the previous schedule of two papers per day).
- **Optional Subject Selection:** Presenter Farah Tariq shared her own winning combination of optionals: International Relations (IR), Environmental Sciences, Criminology, Punjabi, and Public Administration, illustrating how to strategically balance 600 optional marks.

## Crucial Deadlines & Action Items for Students

With the examination timeline fast approaching, attendees were given clear, immediate action items:

- **MPT 2027 Applications:** The application window is open through August 20, meaning candidates targeting CSS 2027 must act swiftly.
- **Exam Window:** The written CSS exams are typically scheduled for January, requiring immediate, disciplined preparation starting right away in mid-August.
- **Resource Sharing:** Farah Tariq committed to sharing essential downloaded resources, including the PMS syllabus, optional subject frameworks, and key FPSC guides, directly within the RAPID WhatsApp and group communication channels.
- **Alternative Pathways:** Students were also introduced to single-paper PPSC/One-Paper exams (with federal equivalents like ASF Inspector roles), noting that negative marking applies under PPSC regulations.

## Looking Forward

The seminar concluded with an energized Q&A and a shared sense of purpose. By connecting current scholars with accomplished alumni mentors like Farah Tariq, RAPID Charity continues to bridge the gap between academic potential and high-level professional success.

RAPID Charity encourages all students and alumni targeting the upcoming exam cycles to monitor the official FPSC and PPSC websites weekly and stay connected through our growing network channels!

posts.title: Giving Back, Moving Forward: RAPID Charity Launches Alumni Network
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: On August 8, 2026, RAPID Charity marked a major milestone by hosting its First Alumni Meeting.
posts.body:
## Introduction & Overview

On **August 8, 2026**, RAPID Charity marked a major milestone by hosting its **First Alumni Meeting**. Organised to strengthen community support, mentorship, and long-term programme sustainability. The virtual gathering brought together dedicated former scholars, Rapid representatives, including **Khushnud Azariah**, **Resha Qadir Bakhsh**, and **Azher Adil**, and passionate alumni from across the region.

Despite technical challenges from adverse weather in Lahore, enthusiasm among participants remained high.

## Key Highlights & Discussions

- **Sustainability:** Discussions centered on how former scholars can support RAPID Charity through international donations (via PayPal) or direct local contributions in Pakistani Rupees.
- **Giving Back Beyond Finances:** Leadership emphasized that time and expertise are just as valuable. Alumni can contribute significantly by mentoring students, teaching, and serving as resource persons.
- **Spotlight on Local Projects:**
  - *Al-Noor School (Rawalpindi):* Providing accelerated primary education, successfully mainstreaming nearly 20 out-of-school children over the past two years.
  - *Sanjha Vehra (Lahore):* Empowering women and youth through vocational skills (stitching, embroidery) with upcoming expansions into computer literacy and digital skills.
- **New Mentorship & Resource Initiatives:** The network established a structured mentorship initiative to pair alumni with current scholars for academic and career guidance.

## Alumni Commitments & Leadership

The alumni response was overwhelmingly positive, with several members immediately stepping up to offer their time and expertise:

- **Farah Tariq** volunteered to conduct a dedicated Zoom webinar on 15 August 2026 for students preparing for CSS and government competitive exams, alongside offering support at the Sanjha Vehra Centre.
- **Shahid Masih** offered to mentor current scholars and leverage his teaching background to support Grades 9, 10, O-Level, and A-Level students at Sanjha Vehra.
- **Abid Arif and Shiraz Kaleem** pledged their active participation in upcoming assignments and alumni activities.

To drive these initiatives forward, a **five-member Alumni Coordination Committee** was established, featuring Shiraz Kaleem, Abid Arif, Farah Tariq, Zakariya, and Shahid Masih. **Shiraz Kaleem** was appointed as the initial Alumni Coordinator for a six-month term.

## Looking Ahead

The newly formed committee is already looking to the future, with planning underway for an exciting **RAPID Charity Alumni and Current Scholar get-together in December 2026**.

RAPID Charity extends its deepest gratitude to all participating alumni for their enduring dedication. Together, we are building a stronger, more supportive community for the next generation of scholars.

> "The meeting concluded on a powerful note of unity, with participants reaffirming their shared commitment to empowering disadvantaged communities through education and mentorship."
posts.imageAlt: Giving Back, Moving Forward: RAPID Charity Launches Alumni Network

posts.title: Scholarship Applications for Spring 2027 Semester Open Now
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Rapid Charity is pleased to announce that applications for its scholarship programs for the Spring Semester 2027 are now open. The deadline for submission is 15 October, 2026.
posts.body:
## Applications Open

Rapid Charity is pleased to announce that applications for its scholarship programs for the Spring Semester 2027 are now open. The deadline for submission is **15 October, 2026**. These scholarships are designed to support students from humble backgrounds who are facing financial hardship and have demonstrated academic excellence with a GPA of 3.5 or higher, or 90% marks.

## Three Scholarship Programs

Rapid Charity offers three distinct scholarships:

1. **John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship:** Open to students pursuing various fields of study, excluding business degrees. It aims to encourage academic excellence and provide financial assistance to those in need.
2. **Robert Mathias Scholarship:** Specifically tailored for students enrolled in business programs, this scholarship supports future business leaders by providing the necessary resources to succeed in their academic and professional endeavors.
3. **Ivy Azariah Scholarship:** In memory of Ivy Azariah, awarded to women focused on developing others; true success measured by skills passed from generation to generation.

## How to Apply

Interested applicants are encouraged to apply online through the Rapid Charity website. For more information on eligibility criteria and the application process, please visit the [Apply](/apply) page.

Rapid Charity is a non-political, non-sectarian, and non-profit organization registered in the United States, committed to serving those in need and promoting career-based higher education among talented young individuals in deprived situations.

For any inquiries, please contact us at info@rapidcharity.org.

*Note: The last date for submitting online scholarship applications for the Spring 2027 Semester is October 15, 2026.*

posts.title: From Scholarship to Success: The Inspiring Journey of Ashar Nadeem
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Read the Story of Ashar Nadeem. How Rapid Charity Scholarship help him to continue his studies.
posts.body:
## A Life Changed by Education

"Education changed my life, and RAPID made it possible." (Ashar Nadeem)

Ashar graduated in 2022 from Forman Christian College (FCC) with a Bachelor's degree in Business Accounting & Finance. Coming from a modest background, with a father working as a driver, a mother managing the household, and three siblings to support. Higher education seemed like a distant dream.

## The Turning Point

When Ashar joined FCC, he received financial aid and work-study opportunities at FCC. Yet, even after these contributions, a significant portion of his tuition fee remained unpaid. The financial pressure became so intense that he was on the verge of freezing his semester.

Through a friend, Ashar learned about **Rapid Charity**. He applied and was awarded a **50% scholarship on his total tuition fee**. RAPID's timely intervention bridged the critical gap his family could not fill. This support allowed him to stay enrolled, concentrate fully on his studies, and graduate without the constant anxiety of unpaid fees.

## Today

Today, Ashar is working as a **Customer Success Executive at Programmers Force**, a well-known technology company. Over the past three years, he has established himself professionally and has been able to fully support his siblings' education. They have now graduated and are employed, a remarkable transformation for the entire family.

Even more inspiring, Ashar and his siblings are now committed to giving back to the community by helping other deserving students gain access to quality education.

> "I am profoundly grateful to the Rapid team for their unwavering backing; without them, none of this would have been possible."

There are many more students like Ashar, talented, hardworking, and determined, who are only one scholarship away from changing their lives.

**Your donation can help another student stay in school, complete their degree, and uplift their entire family.** Support Rapid Charity today: invest in education, transform a future.
posts.imageAlt: From Scholarship to Success: The Inspiring Journey of Ashar Nadeem

posts.title: A Dream Come True: Youas Shaleem’s Story
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Youas Shaleem from Peshawar completed Economics at Edwardes College and is training as a Commissioned Officer at the Pakistan Air Force Academy, with RAPID support.
posts.body:
## Youas Shaleem

We at Rapid Charity are proud to share the inspiring journey of **Youas Shaleem**, a young man from Peshawar who never gave up on his dreams.

Youas is 25 years old and has completed his Bachelor's degree in Economics from Edwardes College, Peshawar. Life was not easy for him. He lost his father in 2010, who worked as a lab technician at LRH Peshawar. Since then, his mother, an amazing woman and now Principal of Edwardes High School, raised him alone and gave him all the support he needed.

He has no siblings, and his mother's strength and hard work shaped him into the person he is today.

## Living the Dream

Today, Youas is training as a **Commissioned Officer** at the **Pakistan Air Force Academy** in Risalpur. Before this, he worked at the **Federal Board of Revenue (FBR)**. Joining the Air Force was his childhood dream, and now, he's living it.

Youas says this would not have been possible without Rapid Charity. We supported his education during tough times, and he stayed focused on his goals. Our help gave him the strength to complete his studies and move forward with confidence.

> "Your support helped me not only get a degree, but also fulfill my dream of joining the Pakistan Air Force. I will always be thankful and will serve my country with the same dedication Rapid showed to me."

We are proud of Youas and wish him all the best in his journey ahead. His story is proof that with a little help and a lot of determination, anything is possible.

Thank you, Youas, for making us proud.
posts.imageAlt: A Dream Come True: Youas Shaleem’s Story

posts.title: Farah Tariq: Story of Empowering Through Education
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Farah Tariq, John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship recipient, now Assistant Director in Punjab's Environment Protection and Climate Change Department.
posts.body:
## Farah Tariq

Rapid Charity proudly presents **Farah Tariq**, a distinguished recipient of the John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship during her academic journey in **BS-Environmental Science (Spring 2021)** and throughout her **PhD program (Spring-Fall 2022 and Spring-Fall 2023)**.

Farah shares how the RAPID scholarship was pivotal in her educational pursuit:

> "With the invaluable support of a RAPID scholarship, I embarked on a remarkable journey toward realizing my dreams. The scholarship not only eased financial burdens but also ignited a flame of ambition within me."

## From Scholar to Public Service

Guided by her strong faith in God and unwavering determination, Farah excelled in her studies and prepared rigorously for competitive government exams. Her dedication paid off as she secured a **BS-17 government position** in the **Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, Punjab**, where she currently serves as an **Assistant Director**.

Farah's story is a testament to the transformative power of education, hard work, and faith. As a government officer, she is now contributing meaningfully to her community and nation, addressing critical environmental and climate change issues with passion and dedication.

> "The RAPID scholarship laid the foundation for my success, providing the resources and encouragement I needed to thrive. My journey underscores the profound significance of trusting God, investing in education, and creating opportunities for aspiring individuals to contribute meaningfully to society."

Farah Tariq's story exemplifies the mission of Rapid Charity: empowering individuals through education to achieve their dreams and make a lasting impact.

posts.title: Maher Mall: A Future Nurse with a Big Heart
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Maher Mall received a RAPID scholarship to study Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) and dreams of serving those who cannot afford care.
posts.body:
## Maher Mall

We are proud to share the story of **Maher Mall**, a hardworking and passionate student who received a scholarship from Rapid Charity to study **Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)**.

Maher comes from a family that believes in hard work and education. Her journey has not been easy, but every challenge made her stronger. She says that success comes with patience, effort, and faith in Allah.

## Her Dream

Her dream is to become a kind and skilled nurse who helps people who cannot afford medical treatment. In Pakistan, many people avoid going to hospitals because they don't have money. Maher wants to change that. She wants to be there for those who need care and support.

> "This scholarship means a lot to me. It gives me hope and pushes me to work even harder. I want to serve my community with love and compassion."

We at Rapid Charity are proud to support students like Maher. Her story reminds us why we do what we do: to help bright minds achieve their dreams and give back to society.

Thank you, Maher, for your dedication. We wish you all the best in your journey to become a nurse and serve the people of Pakistan.

posts.title: Rapid Charity Honored by Forman Christian College University for Supporting Underprivileged Students
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: FCCU honors RAPID Charity for supporting underprivileged students.
posts.body:
## Badge of Honor

*Lahore, November 13, 2025.* Reconciliation and Peace Innovative Development (Rapid) Charity has been honored with the prestigious **Badge of Honor** by **Forman Christian College (A Chartered University)** in recognition of its continued support to students from underprivileged communities.

Forman Christian College (A Chartered University), established in 1864, is one of Pakistan's leading higher education institutions with a strong legacy of academic excellence. FCCU is widely respected for its commitment to nurturing leadership, character, and service within a diverse student community. Nearly 10,000 students are currently pursuing their education at the University.

## Corporate Connect 2025

The award was presented during the **Corporate Connect 2025** event, held at FCCU to celebrate generosity and meaningful partnerships that make higher education more accessible. The Badge of Honor was received on behalf of Rapid Charity by its Chief Executive Officer, **Rev. Dr. Khushnud Azariah**, who has led the organization's efforts to provide educational opportunities for bright and deserving youth.

The recognition highlights Rapid Charity's commitment to empowering marginalized students by enabling them to pursue quality higher education and become active contributors to society. Through scholarships, academic assistance, and mentorship support, Rapid Charity continues to invest in the future of Pakistan's young generation.

## Presentation

The award was presented by **FCCU Rector Dr. Jonathan S. Addleton**, accompanied by FCCU Chief Marketing and Outreach Officer **Badia Raza**, acknowledging the organization's valuable role as a trusted partner in education.

Rev. Dr. Khushnud expressed gratitude for the honor and reaffirmed Rapid Charity's mission: "Education is a powerful tool that transforms lives. We are thankful to FCCU for this recognition and remain committed to ensuring that no talented student is left behind due to financial constraints."

Rapid Charity extends sincere appreciation to Forman Christian College University for this recognition and looks forward to strengthening this partnership for the betterment of students and communities across Pakistan.
posts.imageAlt: Rapid Charity Honored by Forman Christian College University for Supporting Underprivileged Students

posts.title: RAPID Charity's Literacy Program for Out-of-School Children Bearing Fruit
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Literacy program progress for out-of-school children.
posts.body:
## The Challenge

As per the UNICEF report, Pakistan has the world's second-highest number of out-of-school children with an estimated **23 million children aged 5-16** not attending school, representing 44 per cent of the total population in this age group.

## Literacy Program in Mughalabad

Recognizing this alarming situation, RAPID Charity launched Literacy Program for Out-of-School Children on **May 1, 2023** in Mughalabad, Rawalpindi. The program aims to uplift socio-economically marginalized Christian communities by providing basic education to children who otherwise remain deprived due to financial hardships or lack of awareness from their illiterate parents.

This Literacy Center in Mughalabad serves **26 children**, both boys and girls, aged between 5 and 10 years. Two young teachers from the local community, who are also recipients of Rapid Scholarship, conduct classes from Monday to Friday, **8:30 AM to 12:30 PM**.

## Looking Ahead

Looking ahead, the program aims to expand by introducing vocational training for older children. This initiative will equip them with practical skills, enhancing their chances of economic independence and breaking the cycle of poverty.
posts.imageAlt: RAPID Charity's Literacy Program for Out-of-School Children Bearing Fruit

posts.title: How Christmas Inspires Hope & Love in Ordinary Lives
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: A Christmas reflection on hope and love.
posts.body:
## Christmas Message for RAPID Scholars

My dear RAPID scholars,

At Christmas, we celebrate a story that changed the world, not with power or wealth, but with hope and love. Jesus was born in a humble manger to remind us that God often starts His greatest work in unexpected places, with ordinary people…just like us.

Christmas invites us to open our hearts and lives to what God is trying to do in us and through us. When Mary and Joseph arrived in Bethlehem, there was no room for them in the inn. Doors were closed. But the shepherds, simple people, heard the Good News, went to see Jesus, and then joyfully shared what they witnessed.

## Make Room

So, the question for each one of us this Christmas is: **Do we want to be like the innkeeper, so busy and distracted that we have no room for God?** Or will we be like the shepherds, willing to listen, to notice what God is doing, and to take part in God's story?

God is still active in our world. God is still writing the Christmas story, this time through YOU. As RAPID scholarship recipients, you are chosen for a purpose. Your education, your talents, and your dreams can become instruments of God's hope and transformation for your family, for your church and for your country.

But to be part of this story, we must make room:

- Room for compassion, when competition pushes us toward selfishness.
- Room for courage, when challenges seem too big.
- Room for service, when the world tells us to only care for ourselves.
- Room for justice where there is inequality.
- Room for God, in all our plans and priorities.

## The True Test of Christmas

So, the real celebration of Christmas is not about what is under the tree, what clothes we wear, or how beautifully we decorate. The true test of Christmas is: **How much did we open our hearts to let God's love in, and how well did we share that love with others?**

May this Christmas inspire you to shine as light in your families, your colleges, and in your communities. May God's peace guide you. May God's hope strengthen you. And may God's joy fill your hearts.

Merry Christmas! God bless you all. Amen.

**The Revd. Dr. Khushnud Azariah**  
CEO - Rapid Charity
posts.imageAlt: How Christmas Inspires Hope & Love in Ordinary Lives

## Simon Akhtar, RAPID Scholar at FCCU

We are delighted to share the email of Simon Akhtar, a RAPID Scholarship recipient, who is about to completing his degree at Forman Christian College (A Chartered University), Lahore.

Simon expressed his deep gratitude for the financial and moral support that enabled him to continue his higher education. The RAPID Scholarship not only alleviated his financial burdens but also instilled in him the confidence and determination to excel in his studies. Here we are sharing his email with his consent.

## His Letter

Dear RAPID team,

As I near the completion of my degree at Forman Christian College (A Chartered University) Lahore, I want to take a moment and extend my heartfelt gratitude to RAPID for making this dream come true. The RAPID scholarship didn't only support me financially but also gave me confidence and courage to pursue my studies with excellence by maintaining a high GPA every semester.

Moreover, it also helped me make the most of my university experience by excelling in co-curricular activities. For instance, I am serving as president of my University's Education Society, leading a team of around 60 individuals, promoting educational excellence and awareness. I've also represented FCCU in the HEC Athletic Championship twice and hosted many major events at FCCU.

Admittedly, without your support, it would have been impossible for me to complete my degree and achieve this excellence. Your support, love, and care that I have received for the past three years have deeply touched my heart, and I can't wait to replicate this within my community. As an education major, I am eager to contribute to the educational system of Pakistan and work for minority education, after specialization in the same field. I am ready to provide my services as an educationist, teacher trainer, and in planning and social media handling whenever required.

Once again, thank you, Rev. Khushnud Azariah, Ms. Resha Qadir Bakhsh, and the entire RAPID family, for your generosity, love, and support. My academic journey may end at this point, but the impact of your benevolence will stay with me forever, and I will always cherish your matchless contribution towards my academic journey and life goals.

Best Regards,  
Simon Akhtar  
FCCU

---

posts.title: 10 December :Universal Declaration of Human Rights
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Human Rights Day commemorates the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and RAPID’s call to empower marginalized communities through education.
posts.body:
## Human Rights Day

Human Rights Day is observed annually around the world on **10 December**. It commemorates the anniversary of one of the world's most groundbreaking global pledges: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). This landmark document enshrines the inalienable rights that everyone is entitled to as a human being, regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, language, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

The Declaration was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948 and sets out, for the first time, fundamental human rights to be universally protected.

## Key Articles of the UDHR

- **Article 1:** All human beings are born free and equal.
- **Article 2:** Everyone is equal regardless of race, colour, sex, language, religion, politics, or where they were born.
- **Article 3:** Everyone has the right to life (and to live in freedom and safety).
- **Article 4:** Everyone has the right to be free from slavery.
- **Article 5:** Everyone has the right to be free from torture.
- **Article 6:** Everyone has the right to be recognised before the law.
- **Article 7:** We are all equal before the law.
- **Article 8:** Everyone has the right to seek justice if their rights are violated.
- **Article 9:** Everyone has the right to freedom from arbitrary arrest, detention or exile.
- **Article 10:** Everyone has the right to a fair trial.
- **Article 11:** Everyone has the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty.
- **Article 12:** Everyone has the right to privacy and freedom from attacks on their reputation.
- **Article 13:** Everyone has the right to freedom of movement and to be free to leave and return to their own country.
- **Article 14:** Everyone has the right to seek asylum from persecution.
- **Article 15:** Everyone has the right to a nationality.
- **Article 16:** Everyone has the right to marry and to have a family.
- **Article 17:** Everyone has the right to own property.
- **Article 18:** Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion.
- **Article 19:** Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression.
- **Article 20:** Everyone has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.
- **Article 21:** Everyone has the right to take part in government and to have equal access to public service.
- **Article 22:** Everyone has the right to social security.
- **Article 23:** Everyone has the right to work, to equal pay, to protection against unemployment and the right to form and join trade unions.
- **Article 24:** Everyone has the right to rest and leisure.
- **Article 25:** Everyone has the right to a decent standard of living, including food, clothing, housing, medical care and social services.
- **Article 26:** Everyone has the right to education.
- **Article 27:** Everyone has the right to participate in and enjoy culture, art and science.
- **Article 28:** Everyone has the right to a social and international order where the rights in this Declaration can be fully realized.
- **Article 29:** We have a duty to other people and we should protect their rights and freedoms.
- **Article 30:** Nobody can take away these rights and freedoms from us.

## In Pakistan

In Pakistan, the UDHR has laid the foundation for an evolving human rights framework, particularly focusing on vulnerable groups such as women, children and persons with disabilities. As an original signatory to the UDHR in 1948 and subsequently signing seven core human rights treaties, and as a current member of the Human Rights Council, Pakistan has shown a clear political commitment to these universal values.

Empowering marginalized groups with this knowledge is essential for fostering social justice, as it equips them to recognize and challenge discrimination, demand accountability, and access opportunities for a better quality of life. Educated youth can play a pivotal role in promoting awareness of fundamental rights among marginalized communities.

## 2024 Theme: Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now

Human rights can empower individuals and communities to forge a better tomorrow. By embracing and trusting the full power of human rights as the path to the world we want, we can become more peaceful, equal and sustainable.

This Human Rights Day we focus on how human rights are a pathway to solutions, playing a critical role as a preventative, protective and transformative force for good.

posts.title: Anmol's Story: How Rapid Charity Made a Difference
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Anmol Munisha’s journey to Intercultural Theology studies in Göttingen, supported by RAPID Charity.
posts.body:
## Anmol's Journey

Anmol Monisha's story is another example of how Rapid Charity's scholarships are changing lives and shaping futures. A promising young Pakistani girl, Anmol dreamed of pursuing higher education in Intercultural Theology at the University of Göttingen, Germany. Rapid Charity helped make it happen for her.

## Gratitude

In her heartfelt letter to the CEO of Rapid Charity, Anmol expressed her gratitude for the financial support that enabled her to pursue her Master's degree:

> "Your contribution has made a significant difference in my ability to pursue my Master's degree. Your support has alleviated a significant financial burden, allowing me to focus on my studies and achieve my academic goals."

Anmol's words reflect the essence of Rapid Charity's mission: to empower individuals through education and create positive change. She concluded her letter with a promise to "pay it forward and make a difference in the lives of others."

## Looking Forward

Anmol's story is a celebration of resilience, hope, and the transformative power of generosity. At Rapid Charity, we are honoured to be part of her journey and look forward to witnessing the positive impact she will make in the years to come.

Together, we're not just funding education; we're building a brighter future, one student at a time.

Our mission is to provide support to aspiring students, helping them overcome challenges and unlock their potential. Angela John is one of these students. Her remarkable journey from a determined student to a top-ranked graduate in the field of pharmacy is a shining example of how dedication, resilience, and timely support can transform lives.

Throughout this transformative phase, Rapid Charity has stood as a pillar of support, enabling me to reach my aspirations and leaving a positive impact on my life. I am immensely thankful for the invaluable investment Rapid has made in shaping my future.

posts.title: Meet "Samuel Fiaz", recipient of John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Samuel Fiaz completed BS Environmental Sciences at FCCU with John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship support and now studies in the UK.
posts.body:
## Samuel Fiaz

We are excited to share the inspiring journey of **Samuel Fiaz**, a proud recipient of the **John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship**, awarded by Rapid Charity. This scholarship supported Samuel during his academic journey at **Forman Christian College University**, where he completed his **BS in Environmental Sciences** with distinction.

Samuel was awarded the **John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship** for consecutive semesters: **Spring-Fall 2021**, **Spring-Fall 2022**, and **Spring 2023**. This financial assistance played a pivotal role in supporting Samuel to excel in his studies, and explore opportunities for personal growth.

## Beyond FCCU

After completing his Bachelor's degree in 2023, Samuel traveled to the **United Kingdom** to pursue higher education. He is currently enrolled in a **Master's program in Geological and Environmental Sciences** at the **University of Portsmouth**.

Samuel is engaged in a significant research project on **Coastal Erosion in West Sussex**, which addresses critical environmental challenges. Alongside his studies, he is gaining professional experience as a **Buying Administrator** for Bradbeers, a reputable business in Hampshire.

## Gratitude

Samuel expressed heartfelt gratitude for the support of Rapid Charity:

> "I am honored to be a recipient of the John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship. This scholarship has been instrumental in facilitating my academic journey throughout my Bachelor's degree program. It has not only alleviated financial burdens but also served as a source of motivation and encouragement. The support allowed me to focus wholeheartedly on my studies, participate in extracurricular activities, and pursue various academic and personal development opportunities."

Samuel's story exemplifies the impact of the **John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship** and underscores Rapid Charity's commitment to empowering future leaders. Rapid Charity feels proud to have played a role in his journey and wishes him continued success in his endeavors to make a positive impact on the world.

posts.title: Rapid Scholar: Nouman Stephen's story
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Nouman Stephen from Peshawar pursues nursing in Karachi with three-time RAPID scholarship support.
posts.body:
## Peshawar to Karachi

Meet **Nouman Stephen**, a bright and determined young man from **Peshawar, Pakistan**, who set his path in the field of healthcare.

Coming from a Christian family with six siblings, Nouman knows the value of hard work and perseverance. His mother serves patients at **Khyber Teaching Hospital**, while his father contributes through his work as a private medical representative. Inspired by their dedication, Nouman also decided to pursue his dream in healthcare.

## Nursing Studies

Currently, Nouman is a **7th-semester student in the BSN Generic program** at the **Amazing Grace School of Nursing**, affiliated with **Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences (LUMHS)** in Karachi. Pursuing higher education in a different city is not easy, but Nouman proved his resilience.

Thanks to the **RAPID Scholarship Program**, Nouman has received financial support not just once, but **three times**, a gesture that he calls "a true blessing." This support has enabled him to focus on his studies without the burden of financial stress, bringing him one step closer to his dream: becoming a **Master's-level nursing scholar** and a **leader in healthcare**, serving communities that often go underserved.

> "I aim to serve humanity, particularly in my community, including Christians and the surrounding neighborhoods," says Nouman. "This scholarship has given me the strength and opportunity to chase my goals."

## Why It Matters

At Rapid Charity, stories like Nouman's remind us why we do what we do. Every scholarship is more than financial aid. It's an investment in a future caregiver, a changemaker, a community leader.

We are proud to be part of Nouman's journey and look forward to the impact he will make in the years to come.
posts.imageAlt: Rapid Scholar: Nouman Stephen's story

posts.title: RAPID Scholars Get-Together in Kinnaird College
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Thirty John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship recipients gathered at Kinnaird College Haladia Hall on 23 November 2024.
posts.body:
## Gathering at Haladia Hall

Lahore, November 23, 2024 – Thirty John-Ivy Azariah Scholarship recipients gathered for a year-end Christmas celebration at Kinnaird College for Women's Haladia Hall. Despite road closures due to political unrest, the event saw an overwhelming turnout.

The gathering aimed to foster connections among scholars and provide an opportunity to meet Rapid Charity's leadership. The event began with carol singing led by Rapid scholars Shiraz Kaleem and Susana.

## Messages & Sharing

Bishop Samuel Robert Azariah delivered a special Christmas message, highlighting the Magi's visit to Jesus as a symbol of Christ's inclusive message. He emphasized respectful dialogue, building bridges with people of other faiths, and embodying Christ's love.

Scholars shared inspiring experiences, personal stories, and achievements made possible through Rapid Charity. They expressed heartfelt gratitude to RAPID's CEO/President and team.

**Rev. Dr. Khushnud Azariah**, CEO/President of Rapid Charity, emphasized the importance of unity, inspired by Jesus' Priestly Prayer. She highlighted the need to listen to marginalized individuals and work towards building an inclusive society.

**Prof. Dr. Iram Anjum**, Principal of Kinnaird College, congratulated the scholars and praised RAPID's vision. She pledged her full support to RAPID's endeavors.

## Closing

The event concluded with a lunch, providing students with another opportunity to engage in discussions and exchange ideas. The Rapid Charity Annual Report for the year 2024 was also shared through a PowerPoint presentation.
posts.imageAlt: RAPID Scholars Get-Together in Kinnaird College

posts.title: Tabish Raheel and the Rapid Charity Scholarship
posts.author: Communication Desk
posts.excerpt: Tabish Raheel’s Agriculture studies at MNS University Multan supported by RAPID from Spring 2023 to Spring 2025.
posts.body:
## Tabish Raheel

Tabish Raheel, a bright student pursuing a Bachelor of Science (Hons) in Agriculture at Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan. The RAPID Charity Scholarship has supported his educational journey.

Tabish was awarded the RAPID Charity Scholarship, which supported him from **Spring 2023 to Spring 2025**. As he nears the end of his academic career, he reflects on the scholarship's impact on his life, both academically and personally.

## A Moment of Motivation

For Tabish, that motivating moment came in his third semester. He recalls how the RAPID team encouraged him to apply for the scholarship, guiding him to compile his documents and submit his application.

> "I still remember how you motivated me to send my documents for this scholarship when I was in my 3rd semester. It really means a lot," he states in his thank-you message to the RAPID team.

> "Dear Mam and RAPID team, I am really very thankful for helping me out in this whole journey of mine. It wouldn't have been possible without you guys. I am really grateful for your support and efforts and this scholarship," Tabish expresses openly.

Support from organizations like RAPID also builds connections of mentoring and encouragement, which are pivotal in a student's journey.

## Looking Ahead

As Tabish prepares for his final semester in Spring 2025, he feels a sense of excitement and hope for his future.

> "Thank you once again, and God bless you guys and your vision," Tabish ends his heartfelt message.

His sentiment resonates with many who recognize the transformative power of education and the impact of supportive systems in our society. By sharing Tabish's story, we aim to inspire others to seek opportunities that can change their lives.
